competitorFacts.text: ARC Prize named Tufa Labs and its Duck agent the first-place open-source solution for the June 2026 ARC-AGI-3 Milestone 1 prize.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — Duck Harness technical overview
competitorFacts.text: Tufa Labs says its public Duck harness lets an LLM inspect game grids as image and text, write Python in a REPL, and keep context short by evicting older messages. This describes the published Milestone 1 system, not an unverified current submission.
Tufa Labs lists Dries Smit, Isaiah Pressman and Jeroen Cottaar among its AI researchers, with research interests spanning reinforcement learning, self-play and Bayesian methods.

competitorFacts.sourceTitle: Tufa Labs — October 9 public competition post
competitorFacts.text: On October 9, 2026, Tufa Labs described a temporary setback in a public X post and said it remained dedicated to crushing competitors with overwhelming resources and compute.
Yi-Chia Chen’s Kaggle profile lists her as a Competitions Master and a double-degree student at National Taiwan University and Waseda University.

discussionThreads.author: ruichardliu
discussionThreads.reason: Fresh substantive discussion of generalization and learning from failure; expanded branch verified publicly without login.
discussionThreads.summary: Expanded the newest nine-reply branch. Son Pham’s October 19 23:58 UTC reply encourages a participant after a disappointing submission, recounting his own overconfidence in public evaluation and emphasizing completely unseen testing. At October 20 05:26 UTC, CPMP says an earlier ARC-AGI-1 solver went from 75% evaluation to 6% on submission, before his team’s subsequent ARC-AGI-2 win. These are attributed recollections, not new contest scores. Deleted posts remain deleted; a third-party score allegation was not promoted as a verified result.
discussionThreads.title: What are your agents scoring on the 25 public games?

discussionThreads.author: franciseliang
discussionThreads.reason: New substantive participant experiments and negative results; signed-in body/reply read, then verified readable without login.
discussionThreads.summary: Francise Liang reports stopping work and shares tests of Franzen’s public Milestone 2 notebook on an RTX Pro 6000, with 25 public games and two passes per run. Two unchanged runs averaged 47.30 and 48.92; per-game differences had a reported standard deviation of 24 points. Increasing concurrent streams from ten to fourteen reduced the reported mean from 47.30 to 29.90 and throughput; stopping stalled levels at 110k tokens gave 38.97 versus a two-run baseline average of 48.11. Liang recommends repeated comparisons. These are participant measurements on public games, not independently reproduced results or hidden-board scores. Reply author xiaoz259 attributes poor throughput to insufficient KV-cache memory and lane preemption.

socialPosts.author: alin8020
socialPosts.summary: Alan Lin discusses the previously published ARC-AGI-3 standard/provider-adapter results and argues that retaining reasoning between steps matters when choosing a harness.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Fresh public commentary on existing results. Treat as Lin’s interpretation, not a new evaluation or proof that reasoning retention alone caused the difference.

socialPosts.author: gklambauer
socialPosts.summary: Klambauer announces KronLSTM and links the new Kronecker Delta Rule paper. The authors propose a targeted association update for recurrent linear attention, report competitive long-context performance, and link open-source code and models. No ARC score is reported.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Research lead discovered in fses91’s separate Reposts feed. The primary arXiv abstract was checked independently; architecture claims remain attributed, and no Kaggle roster identity is inferred.
